before: 3.1 For $0<\theta_0<\pi$, the angular set $\{\theta=\theta_0\}$ has surface measure zero because its $\theta$-coordinate is a singleton of one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero in [F4]. At $\theta_0=0$ or $\pi$, the angular set is one pole; it is contained in a cap of area $2\pi(1-\cos\varepsilon)$ for each $\varepsilon>0$, and these areas tend to zero. Fubini [F5] on finite radial intervals, followed by their countable union, shows the exact radial cone $\{\theta=\theta_0\}$ is $\nu$-null. A fixed-radius conical shell is a subset and is also null. Every square-integrable field supported on a null set represents the zero Hilbert vector, so the stated ideal mode cannot be normalized. [F4, F5, given, algebra] ∎
